title: A Server with Node and Express
text: These questions check that you can build and test an Express API, serve a page from it, and control who can reach it.

tasks.text: A request arrives for DELETE /signups/42. In the route app.delete("/signups/:id", ...), what is req.params.id?
A POST route reads req.body.email, but req.body is undefined. What's the most likely cause?
choices: app.use(express.json()) is missing, so JSON bodies aren't read

tasks.text: What's the difference between app.listen(3000) and app.listen(3000, "127.0.0.1"), and which should you use while developing on a campus network?
tasks.answer: Without an address, the server listens on all network interfaces, so other devices on the network may reach it; with 127.0.0.1 only your own computer can. Use 127.0.0.1 while developing, especially on shared networks.

tasks.text: The sign-up page disables the button for full shifts. Why must the server still check whether a shift is full?
tasks.answer: Anyone can send a POST request directly (curl, a script) without the page, and two people could sign up at almost the same moment; only checks where the data is stored protect it. The page's check is a convenience.

tasks.text: Write a function checkSignup(email, slot, signups, memberEmails) that returns an object { status, error } for problems, or { status: 201 } if the sign-up is allowed. Rules: missing email → 400; not in memberEmails (compare lowercase) → 400; already signed up → 409; full (signups for the slot ≥ capacity) → 409. signups are { slotId, memberEmail }. Then write testCheckSignup, which logs JSON.stringify for: ("Ava.Lopez@example.com", { id: 6, capacity: 3 }, [], ["ava.lopez@example.com"]) and ("ben.okafor@example.com", { id: 1, capacity: 1 }, [{ slotId: 1, memberEmail: "ava.lopez@example.com" }], ["ava.lopez@example.com", "ben.okafor@example.com"]).

Start with the lesson's server. In a new chat with your updated learner profile, ask for a new route, GET /shifts/:id/spots, that returns only { spotsLeft }. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Does it follow REST and your rules (no emails, 404 for unknown shifts)? (3) Add it, add two test requests to test-api.js (a real shift and an unknown one), run them, and paste the output. (4) Check that the server still listens on 127.0.0.1.
tasks.answer: Full credit: route checked against rules; tests run with correct results (e.g. shift 6 → 3 spots left before any sign-up; 404 for unknown); listening address confirmed. Replies vary, so grade the reasoning.
